children: on Monday announced 12-week induction data from its Phase 2 SWIFT trial evaluating emvistegrast, an investigational once-daily oral treatment for adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.
The biopharmaceutical company revealed the late-breaking findings on Monday at the United European Gastroenterology Week 2026.
The trial evaluated whether the selective oral α4β7 integrin inhibitor, also known as GS-1427, could address the substantial unmet need in inflammatory bowel disease.

The 200 mg dose of emvistegrast met the primary efficacy goal. At Week 12, 66% (39 of 59) of patients receiving the 200 mg dose achieved a clinical response based on the modified Mayo score, compared to 37% (22 of 60) in the placebo cohort.

The candidate also demonstrated statistically significant gains across several secondary endpoints. Approximately 31% (18 of 59) of patients on emvistegrast reached clinical remission, compared with 8% (5 of 60) on placebo.

Furthermore, 39% of participants receiving the 200 mg dose achieved endoscopic improvement versus 12% on placebo. Histological endoscopic mucosal improvement occurred in 25% of emvistegrast patients compared to 10% on placebo, while mucosal healing reached 24% versus 10%.
The patient population included individuals with varied treatment backgrounds. While 78% were naive to advanced therapies or had not failed prior advanced treatments, 22% had previously failed

Emvistegrast demonstrated a generally well-tolerated safety profile during the induction phase. Adverse events occurred in 36% (64 of 178) of emvistegrast participants and 37% (22 of 60) of placebo recipients, with most cases remaining Grade 2 or lower.
Gilead continues the SWIFT study as planned, with upcoming analyses evaluating long-term maintenance outcomes.
Gilead Sciences shares were down 0.75% at $155.02 at the time of publication on Monday,

title: Gilead Bolsters Inflammatory Bowel Disease Pipeline With Promising Mid-Stage Trial Success
